items.quote: "Ok what about the progress knight code what if we used that to replace the arena"  "Yeah I'm saying complelty replace arena"

asks.text: I removed both headers on Haven's page, because you said they compete for space. The words "test prototype, trial numbers" are still read out to screen readers, and the help (?) still says the numbers are trial values. They're just no longer shown at the top.

The town's tiles now grow to at most 44px, up from 40px and usually 32px. Past that, the edges of the map go off screen and you drag to see them. I think that's the right balance. Bigger tiles would mean dragging more.
An open drawer section is at most about a fifth of the screen's height (92–280px), and its list scrolls inside it. I'd keep it short like this, so the town stays the main thing on screen.

I left the handheld frame as it is (5px sides, an 18px top strip). It costs about 28px of height. If the town still feels cramped, the top strip could shrink to the same 5px as the sides, but I'd try this first.

On the smallest phone (320×610), Haven doesn't fit with a section open. The list shows about one row, cut off at the bottom of the frame, and you have to drag on the counters to bring the rest into view. I'd hide the two lines under the town while a section is open, so it fits.
On the smallest phone, tapping Hide makes the town's tiles smaller (32px to 24px), though the town gets more room. I'd work out the tile size from the room the town really gets.
On the smallest phone, the Defense tab reads "Defe…". I'd use 12px letters on the tabs there.

asks.text: The lunge now repeats every 4 seconds, the same timing as the tutorial, and a tap plays it at once. I think it suits the page. If it feels busy while you read stats, 6 seconds would be calmer.

items.title: Double species mastery summon requirements and damage bonuses
items.quote: Make mastery’s take twice as many summons and twice as more powerful.

asks.text: Look at the mastery text on a phone in a local browser at 320×610, 375×667, 390×844 and 430×932: the Party companion page, the Team page, the summon result and the Omnidex. Check that "+48%" and "120 summons" fit without overflowing.
If #89 or #98 (new rarities for the roster) adds mastery totals for more rarities, double those too when they merge, so every rarity follows the same rule.

Mastery now takes twice the summons for each rank (table above) and gives +8% damage per rank, up to +48% at Mastery VI. I think the bigger bonus is a good trade for the longer climb. Doubling the Common totals makes Mastery VI need 120 summons, which is a long grind for Commons.

Existing players drop ranks under the new totals, as you chose. A player who had Mastery VI on a Common with 60 summons will see Mastery IV. A short "mastery has changed" note in the game could stop that feeling like a bug. I haven't added one; it's your call.

The Hall trophy "The Sixfold Covenant" (Mastery VI in each of the six families) is worked out fresh from the current ranks. So a player who had it could see it locked again until they reach the new totals. It gives no reward, so nothing is taken back. "The Last Vigil" stays unlocked, because the game already remembers that one once it's earned.
It clashes with another change in progress, in team.js, so it isn't on the test site yet.
